page: Amazon Web Services c8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The server is powered by AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.7 GHz across 192 physical cores, with single-threaded core execution providing 192 dedicated virtual CPUs. Memory resources total 384 GB of DDR5 RAM, matching a compute-focused ratio of 2 GB per core. The bare-metal platform features no hypervisor layer, no local storage volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps. Acceleration hardware is omitted, with zero dedicated GPUs installed.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded execution and memory throughput. The platform achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 301,702.93 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 21,200.0, both placing in the top ten percent. High-volume parallel execution is further reflected in Clang software compilation benchmarks (88,519.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1,042.65 GB/sec). Large-block read memory bandwidth reaches 909.22 GB/sec uncached, with write throughput measured at 404.46 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into median percentiles, including Geekbench single-core at 1,658.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1,648.58.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core density delivers substantial multi-threaded throughput per resource allocation without the overhead of virtualization. However, tradeoffs include the lack of bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures, and lower token-generation rates in large language model inference due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators or discrete GPUs.

Amazon Web Services c8g.metal-48xl is structurally suited for highly parallel compute workloads, large-scale software compilation, distributed caching nodes such as Redis (reaching 353.35 million SET operations per second), high-throughput static web serving, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.7 GHz and 384 GB of DDR5 memory. The instance features a compute-oriented ratio of 2 GB per core and provides a 50 Gbps network baseline without integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top decile for multi-threaded processing, evidenced by high throughput across Geekbench multi-core, Clang compilation, and parallel bzip3 decompression tasks. Memory bandwidth is similarly elevated, reaching 909.22 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. While single-thread execution is moderate, the high core density yields exceptional efficiency for horizontally parallel operations. This instance is best suited for large distributed caches, software compilation clusters, high-concurrency web serving, and compute-heavy batch workloads.
